extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers, NIH-funded investigators, grant-policy advocates and analysts interested in racial disparities in NIH funding
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and policy proposals for correcting racial disparities in NIH R01/RPG funding rates, using Hoppe et al. (2019) data to estimate numbers of unfunded Black-PI applications and the portfolio impact of funding them. Includes methods for allocating needed funds across NIH institutes and for assessing effects on white PI success rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund every scored application from African-American PIs (policy proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The NIH should fund every scored application submitted by African-American PIs, reaching back 2 years and into the future for 5 years." (Twitter poll / stated policy prescription)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a concrete remedial policy to immediately address disparity; author uses Hoppe et al. data to show the numerical and portfolio impact. Treated as a thought experiment/policy option rather than the only solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use triage/discussed/funded counts as the basic accounting framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Count applications by outcome categories (triaged/not discussed, discussed-but-unfunded, and funded) using Hoppe et al.'s R01 application data (FY2011–2015): e.g., 2403 Black-PI R01 applications, 1346 triaged (56%), 1057 discussed (44%), 256 funded (≈10.7%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer referencing Table S1 in the Hoppe supplement rather than Figure 1 (Figure 1 confuses applicants with applications). Be mindful of rounding errors when converting percentages to counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate unfunded Black-PI applications to ICs proportionally by NIH$ share
rubrics_metrics.description: When estimating per-institute counts of triaged/discussed-unfunded Black-PI applications, allocate the national unfunded applications proportionally to each NIH Institute/Centre's share of NIH appropriations (e.g., NCI 15.5% → estimated 42 NDs and 25 discussed-unfunded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a pragmatic way to distribute estimated needed funds across ICs when PI race-by-IC data are not available; acknowledges limitations because % Black PIs likely vary across ICs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust estimates to IC portfolio size (type 1 and type 2 grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Express the required additional funded applications as a percentage of an IC's current new (type 1) and renewal (type 2) grants to understand portfolio impact (examples: NIGMS 2% of funded portfolio; NIMH 2.7%; NIDA 5.2%; NIAAA 2.5%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps IC leadership see the relative magnitude of adjustments; round appropriately and note that the metric uses current FY counts and therefore is forward-looking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of small absolute numbers per IC/year
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated per-IC per-year unfunded Black-PI applications are small (approx ~11 triaged and ~6 discussed-but-unfunded per IC per year in the author's proportional calculation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small absolute numbers mean modest practical changes at the IC level, but still meaningful for affected applicants; caution because small-n variability and unknown IC-level PI racial composition weaken precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify the effect on white PI success rates when funding Black-PI applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute how funding X Black-PI applications would change the national success rate for white PIs (examples given: funding 801 discussed Black-PI apps and subtracting 801 white-PI-funded apps would change white PI success from 17.7% to 16.9%; funding 169 apps to equalize overall rates would drop white PI success from 17.7% to 17.5%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this calculation to counter zero-sum objections by showing the small percent change to white PI success rates relative to the disparity to be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target parity in success rates between Black and white PIs (measure required change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate how many grants would need to be shifted/funded to close the observed success-rate gap (author notes that <0.2% change in white PI success would fix a 7.0% deficit in Black-PI success rates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame parity as an achievable, small-impact adjustment on the majority population's success rate; use precise counts from dataset to quantify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for topic distribution effects on funding (Hoppe finding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that Black PIs are overrepresented in certain research topic clusters that are themselves disadvantaged in review outcomes; Hoppe focuses on topic words and research interests as a mechanism producing disparity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While topic distribution explains some disparity, author emphasizes that Black PIs remain disadvantaged even within topic clusters—so topic-based remedies alone may be insufficient; include topic-cluster analyses but do not treat them as the whole story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider historical/contextual differences (established vs new PIs; renewals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful that aggregate RPG or R01 hit rates conflate established vs new investigators and competing renewals vs new grants; historically, established PIs and renewal applications had higher success rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting past success rates or designing remedies, disaggregate by investigator status and application type if possible; historical high-success cohorts influence perceived fairness and accumulated advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate data sources and prefer tables over potentially misleading figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer specifically to Hoppe et al. (2019) and its Supplement (Table S1) for accurate counts; avoid relying on Figure 1 which may conflate applicants and applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check whether counts are applicants vs applications; watch rounding inconsistencies when converting proportions to raw counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame policy discussion to avoid simplistic zero-sum perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Argue against the mindset 'I'm exchanging my grant for their grant' by demonstrating that the percent changes required for parity are small for the majority group and large in consequence for the disadvantaged group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use numerical examples to show trade-offs concretely; emphasize relative vs absolute impacts to shift conversation from individual loss to systemic correction.
